$schema.note: Mechanical facts (counts, routes, endpoints, dependencies) are read from source at run time. Purpose strings are curated. Unverifiable items carry status UNKNOWN or confidence low.

project.name: UI HUB
project.purpose: A component and template marketplace for "vibe coding": browsable, copyable React/Three.js UI components, website-section templates, an MCP server and a CLI for AI coding agents, with free/pro/custom monetisation via Razorpay.

deploymentTargets.serves: frontend SPA + /api serverless wrapper around the backend
one web service running the backend with the MCP routers mounted in-process

project.structure: Non-workspace monorepo: frontend, backend, mcp-server, cli, api wrapper, scripts.

frontend.name: react-example
frontend.state: React Context (auth, theme, cookie consent, skeleton) + Zustand (CloudScroll only) + localStorage entitlement mirror
analytics: Google gtag.js with Consent Mode v2 defaults denied
frontend.testing: NONE — the frontend has no test suite and no test script. `npm run lint` is `tsc --noEmit`.
frontend.linting: tsc --noEmit only. No ESLint or Prettier config present.

backend.name: ui-hub-backend

scripts.build: cd ../mcp-server && npm install && npm run build

backend.cache: Redis — ioredis + @upstash/redis for distributed rate limiting
backend.payments: razorpay 2 server SDK + HMAC signature verification
backend.email: Brevo (primary), with Nodemailer SMTP and Resend fallbacks
backend.testing: node:test — `npm test` runs check:premium then node --test tests/

mcpServer.name: ui-hub-mcp-server
mcpServer.protocol: JSON-RPC 2.0, hand-implemented. The official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is NOT a dependency.
mcpServer.capabilities: tools only — no resources/* or prompts/* methods are implemented
mcpServer.auth: SHA-256-hashed API keys in MongoDB, plus Firebase ID tokens for the dashboard API and an admin-email allow-list for the admin API

cli.name: ui-hub-cli

scripts.test: node --import tsx --test tests/config.test.ts tests/mcp.test.ts tests/args.test.ts tests/output.test.ts

cli.dependencies: ZERO runtime dependencies (only devDeps: typescript, tsx, @types/node)
cli.transport: MCP JSON-RPC over HTTP. The CLI does not call the REST backend.
cli.testing: node:test via tsx — config, mcp, args, output

frontendHtml.purpose: HTML shell. Sets title, OG/Twitter/Schema.org meta, Google site-verification, Google Fonts, and loads gtag.js with Consent Mode v2 defaults set to denied.

frontendRoot.purpose: Frontend entry. Calls initFirebase() with a hardcoded fallback config literal, mounts React, then fetches /api/v1/config/firebase and discards the response.

frontendRouter.purpose: Root router and app shell. All 60 <Route> elements live here, plus shell chrome visibility rules, theme classes and the mount-time background sync trigger.

backendServer.purpose: Backend entry. Mounts one router at BOTH /api and /, then dynamically imports and mounts the MCP routers at /mcp, /api/dashboard/mcp and /api/admin/mcp. Sets Helmet CSP, trust proxy, and the global rate limiter.

vercelApiFunction.purpose: Vercel serverless entry. Re-exports the Express app from backend/src/server.js as a default export so /api/* resolves to the whole backend.

mcpHttp.purpose: HTTP entry. Mounts the mcp, dashboard and admin routers at the same three paths the backend uses.

mcpStdio.purpose: stdio entry. Runs with an implicit admin identity for local desktop clients.

cliEntry.purpose: CLI entry. Only login, config and logout are exempt from the API-key requirement.

databaseConnection.purpose: MongoDB connection for the backend. Reached indirectly through backend services.

authEntry.purpose: The single exported middleware, verifyToken, which validates a Firebase ID token.

deployEntry.purpose: Backend + MCP deploy definition for Render.

authentication.mechanism: Firebase Authentication for users; SHA-256-hashed API keys for MCP clients; an email allow-list for admin.

userFlow.signup: firebase/auth createUserWithEmailAndPassword (or Google signInWithPopup) → AuthContext syncs the user to POST /api/v1/users/sync → GET /api/v1/users/status populates entitlements.
userFlow.session: Firebase ID token, browserLocalPersistence. getIdToken() is attached as an Authorization: Bearer header by the frontend clients.
userFlow.refresh: Entitlements are re-fetched on window focus and visibilitychange, throttled to 30s, and once per session on auth-state change.
userFlow.offline: On network failure AuthContext PRESERVES the cached localStorage entitlements rather than clearing them.

admin.mechanism: Firebase ID token, then requireAdmin checks the email against MCP_ADMIN_EMAILS. Routes are under /api/admin/mcp.

clientSideBypass.detail: AuthContext hardcodes three email addresses that bypass category and component access checks in the UI, and forces isPro for one of them. Client-side only — server-side enforcement is what actually matters. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md; NOT modified in this phase.

authentication.secrets: No credential values are recorded in this knowledge base. Env var NAMES only.

flow: frontend: GET /api/v1/config/razorpay-key to obtain the publishable key
frontend: load https://checkout.razorpay.com/v1/checkout.js and open the checkout
frontend: POST /api/v1/payment/verify-payment with the Razorpay response
backend: HMAC-SHA256 signature verification via timingSafeEqual in utils/verifySignature.js
backend: entitlement is granted and mirrored to the client by GET /api/v1/users/status
payments.webhook: POST /api/v1/payment/webhook is registered on the RAW body before express.json, and is not authenticated by a user token. Requires Phase-level review.

plan.constraint: planId and tier are validated to "pro" only; currency to INR or USD only

payments.unlock: Purchased component ids are returned by GET /api/v1/users/status and mirrored to localStorage by AuthContext.

items.finding: The CORS origin callback logs "Blocked origin" and then still returns callback(null, true), so the allow-list does not actually block anything.
POST /v1/users/push-broadcast has no verifyToken middleware, as do the broadcast and email-test endpoints. Same for the sibling broadcast routes.
A Firebase web config is hardcoded as a literal fallback and is the config that actually ships — the runtime config fetch response is discarded and the re-init call is commented out.
Three hardcoded email addresses bypass category and component access checks client-side, and one forces isPro.
GET /logs is registered twice; the first handler wins and the second is dead code.
mcp-server/dist is explicitly un-ignored and committed. It is load-bearing at runtime but can silently drift from src.
vite, @vitejs/plugin-react and @types/three are declared in dependencies rather than devDependencies. @splinetool/*, simplex-noise and unicornstudio-react are declared but not imported anywhere.
Orphaned data: claudePrompts.ts (~95KB, 10 entries, no importer), embeddedSourceCode.ts.bak (~881KB, no importer).
No catch-all 404 route. Unknown paths render an empty main element.
On network failure entitlements are preserved from cache rather than cleared. Intentional offline behaviour, but it means a revoked entitlement can persist locally.
